claims.statement: The 2024 Verizon DBIR reports 1,997 basic web application attack incidents and 881 with confirmed data disclosure, and states that threat actors continue to take advantage of assets with default, simplistic, and easily guessable credentials via brute forcing them, buying them, or reusing them from previous breaches. The word 'continue' supports persistence of an observed threat pattern; the record does not report a temporal increase or decrease in brute-force-specific incident count or frequency (NoI).

Mandiant M-Trends 2024 reports that in 2023 exploit was the most prevalent identified initial infection vector at 38%, a six percentage point increase from 2022; phishing was 17%, down from 22% in 2022; prior compromise was 15%; and brute force appears in the initial-infection-vector chart data with a 6% value (chart-data-only, not an explicitly narrated brute-force NoI trend). These vector shares describe proportions when the initial vector was identified and do not constitute a brute-force-specific incident-count (NoI) time series.

Mandiant M-Trends 2024 describes attackers performing password guessing against cloud sign-in portals to identify accounts without MFA, along with related credential-abuse behaviors including MFA push notification approval abuse, help-desk and technical-support social engineering, and targeted SIM swapping to obtain SMS-based MFA or account-recovery codes.

IBM X-Force 2023 reports that, in OT-related industries, widespread and likely indiscriminate internal and external vulnerability scanning was the most common attack attempt, that old vulnerabilities and threats such as WannaCry and Conficker remain relevant, and that the discussion references vulnerabilities that make brute force attacks easier for attackers.

The Crossref cutoff-constrained publication trend for IDS/IPS security reports annual publication counts of 44 in 2021, 43 in 2022, 52 in 2023, and 58 in 2024, with an OLS slope of 5.1 works/year and a first-to-last delta of 14. The record explicitly states that this publication-activity axis does not establish deployment maturity, operational effectiveness, or causal mitigation effectiveness.

CISA CPG and NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 describe MFA with hardware-based phishing-resistant methods ranked highest, unique credential provisioning for IT and OT assets, alerting after consecutive unsuccessful login attempts, system-enforced login prevention or automatic account lockout, and alternative actions to help prevent brute force attacks, mapped to brute-force subtechniques T1110.001 through T1110.004. The supplied records do not state exact control effectiveness.
